newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy plans late-night summer museum openings.
newsitem.headline: Italy plans late-night summer museum openings.

text.p: Some of Italy's most popular museums and archaeological sites will open until almost midnight for three nights a week over the summer tourist season, under a scheme dubbed "art under the stars" by the government.

The late-night opening will cover 33 museums and sites, including the Uffizi art gallery in Florence, Rome's Borghese Gallery and the Capodimonte Museum in Naples, the culture ministry said on Wednesday.

The scheme runs from June 19 until September 14. Over that period, the venues involved will re-open from 8.30 to 11.30 p.m. on Thursdays, Fridays and Saturdays following a 90-minute closure for cleaning.
The scheme does not include the Roman ruins in Pompeii and those of the Forum, Palatine Hill and Colosseum in Rome because of insufficient lighting, officials said.
